properties.decision:
SETTLED ON ANTHONY'S WORD, 2026-08-15: option (c), split the axis. He was shown four options and chose the one that addresses the pattern rather than the loudest instance.

DISTINCT FROM its two neighbours by design: the FACT measures the problem and counts its occurrences; the IDEA held the four unmade options; THIS records the choice and what was built.

WHAT WAS BUILT, the same day:
· `ChangeSubject { System, Record }` — a new OPTIONAL property on ChangeEvent. Absent means nobody said and is NEVER inferred from `change_type`, because the mapping is not total: a `resync` can be either.
· `ChangeType::DefectFix` — 'the design was right and the code was wrong', distinct from `TestFailureFix`, which is the same repair with different PROVENANCE (a check caught it). That difference is one this project already cares about everywhere else.
· Both reachable from `add_change_event`, and the tool description now says the two questions are two questions.
· The two internal call sites now STATE their axis: a `design_holds` accept is `system` (the file moved; the move carried no design meaning), and a first baseline is `record` — the case the axis was named for. `record_change` passes None on purpose: the generic path cannot know, and a guess would be a claim nobody made.

⭐ THE SPLIT WAS ALREADY NAMED IN THE CODE AND LEFT UNUSABLE, which is the whole argument. `BaselineEstablished`'s own doc comment reads: 'the odd one out, and deliberately so. Every other variant answers why the THING changed; this one says the thing did not change and only the design's KNOWLEDGE of it did.' An axis with exactly one member, reserved so nobody could reach it — and five forced choices followed.

THE EVIDENCE, and the count is the argument: five sessions, four people, three projects, two independent tool surfaces. `chg:duplicate-merge-needs-a-human-20260808` and `chg:accept-acb06c45b63a7b6d` used `test_failure_fix` where no test existed; `chg:arrival-delta-decided` used `scope_change` to mean 'an open question was settled'; Alex tried `bugfix`, was refused, and wrote 'the enum forces a lie'; and the edit recording his report used `resync` to mean 'our knowledge moved and the thing did not'. THE SAME MISSING MEANING WAS ABSENT FROM `set_artifact_checksum`'s DISPOSITION TOO — one absence is a wording gap, two independent absences of one category is a category the vocabulary did not have.

PROVEN: 5 tests, MUTATION-CHECKED TWICE, each killing exactly one counterweight. Defaulting an unstated axis to `system` kills only `an_unstated_axis_stays_unstated`. Deriving the axis from `change_type` kills only `one_change_type_appears_on_both_axes` — the test that pins `Resync` appearing on BOTH axes, which is why the mapping cannot be inferred. The reserved-value counterweight holds throughout: `baseline_established` is still `set_artifact_checksum`'s alone.

📌 THE STAMP DOES NOT MOVE, verified rather than assumed: `GraphStamp` carries type NAMES and COUNTS only — no properties, no enum values — so both halves are invisible to it and NO UPGRADE DOC IS OWED. The flip side is worth knowing and is the stamp's blind spot again: a consumer cannot learn from the stamp that a property appeared.

NOT SETTLED: whether anything should READ `subject` — it is expressible now and nothing computes from it, which is this project's own recurring 'declared and read by nothing' risk, taken knowingly. And 'an open question was settled' still has no `change_type` value; the axis now lets `resync`+`record` say it honestly, which may be enough or may not.
properties.name: `change_type` answers WHY; a new `subject` answers WHICH AXIS — the system changed, or only the design's knowledge of it did
properties.rationale: Recorded as his ruling with what was built attached, so a later reader sees the choice and its consequence in one place. He chose (c) over (a) after the evidence showed at least three missing meanings rather than one — adding a single value would have fixed the loudest case and left the mechanism that produced all five.
